model_choice.chosen: near-unit-root AR(1), rho = 1 - delta, innovation sd eps; plus ARFIMA(0,d,0)
model_choice.why: the compendium's pair (eps = amplitude, delta = memory rate) with a metric eps^2/delta^3 is the signature of a Lorentzian/Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spectral density eps^2/(delta^2 + lambda^2), whose exact discrete-time analogue is the near-unit-root AR(1). Long memory is delta -> 0. ARFIMA(0,d,0) is included as the cleanest long-range-dependent alternative, where the Whittle information for d is analytically pi^2/6 per observation.
model_choice.estimator: Whittle likelihood on the periodogram, innovation variance profiled out analytically

ARFIMA_d.verdict: PASS; and it independently exhibits 'memory is free' in its cleanest form -- the variance of d_hat does not depend on d at all

delta_exponent.note: converging to +1 as n grows; the residual shortfall at small n is the near-unit-root finite-sample effect (n*delta small)

eps_dependence.claimed: Var proportional to 1/eps^2, i.e. ratio 1/6.25 = 0.16 when eps goes 1.0 -> 2.5

claim_b_variance_3_delta3_over_n_eps2.exact_structural_reason: in any spectral model of the form f = eps^2 * g(lambda; delta) the amplitude enters log f additively, so d(log f)/d(delta) is free of eps and the Fisher information for delta cannot depend on eps. The claimed variance formula is therefore not the variance of any memory-rate estimator in an amplitude-scaled family, independently of the simulation.

claim_a_metric_eps2_over_delta3.verdict: NOT the Whittle/Fisher metric for delta
claim_a_metric_eps2_over_delta3.note: the two claims (a) and (b) are individually wrong but wrong reciprocally, which is why their product survives -- see below

with_the_claimed_metric.verdict: NOT FLAT. Spans four orders of magnitude in delta and scales with eps^2. As literally stated with the two named inputs, the floor is not 3/(2n).

with_the_true_metric_one_parameter.note: entries are n = 1024, 4096, 16384; each row converges to 0.500 as n grows, the deviation being the near-unit-root finite-sample effect
with_the_true_metric_one_parameter.verdict: FLAT AT 1/2, i.e. the floor is 1/(2n) for a one-parameter model, uniformly in delta

three_parameter_arm.model: AR(1) with unknown (rho, innovation variance, mean)

claim_c_transported_floor_3_over_2n.resolution: the conclusion 3/(2n) uniformly in delta is CORRECT, and the constant 3 is the parameter count, not anything about memory. When the loss is the Fisher metric, an efficient estimator gives expected transported loss exactly p/(2n) for p parameters, by reparameterisation invariance -- delta and eps cancel because ANY parameterisation's factors cancel. The stated mechanism (a specific metric eps^2/delta^3 against a specific variance 3 delta^3/(n eps^2)) is the right shape with the wrong contents: the two named inputs are each wrong, and the '3' that the theorem attributes to the variance formula is really the dimension of the model.

claim_d_does_the_variance_blow_up_as_mem.verdict: RESOLVED: prose and formula are talking about different quantities, and longMemoryVariance_strictMono correctly records the absolute direction

absolute_variance.direction: shrinks as delta -> 0, matching the stated formula and the Lean lemma

relative_precision.direction: blows up as delta -> 0, by a factor of 300 in Var(log) over this range

claim_d_does_the_variance_blow_up_as_mem.reading: the upstream prose is describing relative (log-scale) precision, which does blow up; the formula is an absolute variance, which shrinks. Both are right about their own quantity. Note the scale: at delta = 0.005 and n = 1024 the relative sd exceeds 1, so the memory parameter is not identified at all there even though its absolute variance is the smallest in the table.

what_survives: the headline: the transported estimation floor really is flat in the memory parameter, and really is 3/(2n) for a three-parameter model. Measured 1.4969 to 1.5151 across delta from 0.4 to 0.1 at n = 65536.
transportedFloor_eq and transportedFloor_indep_of_memory are algebra and are correct as algebra
longMemoryVariance_strictMono correctly reports which way the stated formula runs
what_fails: the metric field eps^2/delta^3 is not the Fisher information for a memory rate; the true one is 1/(2 delta) and cannot depend on eps
the variance field 3 delta^3/(n eps^2) is wrong in the delta exponent (3 vs measured 1) and in the eps dependence (1/eps^2 vs none)
the attribution of the constant 3 to the variance formula. It is the parameter count.
what_could_not_be_tested: whether the upstream derivation has some other parameterisation in which eps^2/delta^3 IS the information; only the natural spectral parameterisations were simulated
genuinely continuous-time observation schemes, where a different metric could arise
the minimax claim itself as opposed to the efficiency-based floor: the simulation bounds the Whittle estimator's risk, not the minimax risk over all estimators
